Business goal: Create a durable tenant record with stable business identity and display name.
User outcome: A root operator can create a new tenant without direct database access.
Notes / constraints: System generates tenant UUID and standard audit/lifecycle timestamps. Client must supply bizId, name, category, and status only. bizId is mandatory, durable, immutable after create, and unique on normalized value. category and status are explicit durable tenant fields so future business rules can bind to them. Standard system fields are server-managed. Initial draft excludes automatic tenant-admin or tenant-user bootstrap side effects.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant admins; tenant users; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without RootUserAdmin
Authorization summary: Tenant creation is restricted to privileged root operators holding the RootUserAdmin boundary.
Frontend visibility rule: Future admin shell may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam before tenant feature service execution.
Request contract: Body includes bizId, name, category, and status only. Client-supplied id, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt, version fields, or other system-managed fields are rejected. bizId and name must be non-empty after trim. category must be one of customer, demo, or test. status must be one of draft, live, disabled, or inactive.
Response contract: Returns created tenant with tenantId UUID, bizId, name, category, status, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt=null, and any approved lifecycle/status fields.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing tenant.create; 409 normalized bizId already exists; 422 category, status, lifecycle, or normalization rule violation.
Search / filter model: 400 invalid payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing tenant.create; 409 normalized bizId already exists; 422 lifecycle or normalization rule violation.
Compatibility / migration notes: Potential future seam to bootstrap tenant-scoped auth or membership should stay explicit and out of v1 create unless approved.
CSP / browser security impact: Primary key on tenantId UUID. Unique index on normalized active bizId. Optional secondary index on normalized name if later list/search requirements approve it.
Audit requirement: Exact reads by tenantId and list/search by bizId/name prefixes if approved. No comma-separated or JSON search shortcuts.
Privacy / personal data impact: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and root-role authorization boundary.
Standards impact: Backward-compatible additive feature. Do not infer durable tenant identity from mutable related records. Keep tenant business identity on the tenant record itself. Initial implementation remains tenant-record-only and defers tenant-admin bootstrap to a later slice.
ADR required?: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Test-case doc required?: No special browser/CSP impact beyond existing protected API/browser console posture.
Feature docs update required?: Audit all successful creates and denied attempts with actor, tenantId when created, bizId, timestamp, and relevant request metadata.
Runbook required?: Moderate; tenant name and business identifier are durable business records and may be sensitive organizational metadata.
Standards review required?: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status review expected because this introduces a new durable business entity.
Acceptance notes: Server must generate tenant UUID and timestamps, reject duplicate normalized bizId values consistently across validation and persistence, and persist category/status as explicit durable tenant fields.

User outcome: A root operator can deactivate a tenant without erasing historical records.
Notes / constraints: Soft delete sets deletedAt and refreshes updatedAt. Normal read/list/update paths exclude deleted rows. This capability should not physically remove tenant-linked data. Tenant category and status remain durably stored and visible through explicit deleted-read/list paths.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant admins; tenant users; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without RootUserAdmin
Authorization summary: Tenant soft-delete is restricted to RootUserAdmin in the first draft.
Frontend visibility rule: Future admin shell may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam before tenant feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact tenantId UUID required. No client-supplied lifecycle timestamps accepted.
Response contract: Returns tenant summary with category, status, deletedAt set, and updatedAt refreshed.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing tenant.delete; 404 tenant not found; 409 already deleted or protected lifecycle rule violation.
Persistence impact: Soft-delete tenant row and preserve durable history.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on deletedAt and normalized active bizId should support active-only uniqueness and deleted-row filtering.
Search / filter model: Deleted rows excluded from normal search/list; explicit deleted-read/search remains separate from active paths.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and root-role authorization boundary.

Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
CSP / browser security impact: No special browser/CSP impact beyond existing protected API/browser console posture.

Business goal: Reactivate a soft-deleted tenant while preserving durable history.
User outcome: A root operator can restore a soft-deleted tenant to active visibility without recreating it.
Notes / constraints: Reactivation clears deletedAt and refreshes updatedAt. The tenant resumes normal read/list/update visibility after reactivation. category and status remain durable fields; reactivation restores the record without inventing a new tenant identity.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant admins; tenant users; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without RootUserAdmin
Authorization summary: Tenant soft-delete is restricted to RootUserAdmin in the first draft.
Frontend visibility rule: Future admin shell may expose this only from deleted-tenant views to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam before tenant feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact tenantId UUID required. No client-supplied lifecycle timestamps accepted. Optional reason/notes field may be added later if policy requires it.
Response contract: Returns tenant summary with tenantId, bizId, name, category, status, deletedAt=null, and updatedAt refreshed.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing tenant.reactivate; 404 deleted tenant not found; 409 tenant is not deleted or reactivation blocked by lifecycle/business rule.
Persistence impact: Clear deletedAt on existing tenant row and preserve durable history.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on deletedAt and normalized active bizId should support moving the tenant back into the active uniqueness set safely.
Search / filter model: Reactivated rows reappear in normal active list/read paths and leave deleted-only list/read paths.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and root-role authorization boundary.
Compatibility / migration notes: If soft delete exists, reactivation is the compatible inverse lifecycle action. Ensure normalized active bizId uniqueness is still enforced when reactivating a previously deleted tenant.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
CSP / browser security impact: No special browser/CSP impact beyond existing protected API/browser console posture.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful reactivations and denied attempts with actor, tenantId, prior deletedAt state, timestamp, and reason if supplied.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; restores visibility of durable organizational metadata.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; recoverability and compliance posture should be reviewed for lifecycle retention semantics.
Acceptance notes: Reactivation must preserve tenant identity, clear deletedAt, refresh updatedAt, and fail safely if active-record uniqueness or lifecycle rules would be violated.
